USGS Astrogeology Science Center · NASA / ESA · Fergason et al. (2018) · Marswalk DEM derivatives · 200 m nominal posting blending Mars Express HRSC and MGS MOLA elevation observations. 600 m north gradient support for derivatives. Neither posting nor support establishes effective spatial resolution or absolute accuracy; absolute positional and slope uncertainty unmeasured. Coarse regional baseline; small rocks, boulders, and local rover/suit hazards are completely unresolved. Not for astronaut hazard or safety routing.

Coverage: Original source is a global HRSC–MOLA product; Marswalk serves a localized Gale-area crop, about 35.28 × 47.20 km (1,665.252534 km²), not a complete Gale Crater map. All 41,772 derived cells valid; covers the fixed optical overview. Outside crop transparent. CTX/color alignment remains unverified.

Native PDS grid 1 m, mixed HiRISE/CTX lineage without per-pixel quality. Heights in metres above the MOLA areoid. Absolute horizontal/vertical accuracy and slope error unquantified. Local orthophoto/CTX comparison indicates a possible positional mismatch; no fitted shift applied. Full-opacity independent DEM view by default. Coverage: Audited 1 km projected square in the historical Curiosity corridor, 137.371118..137.387989 E, -4.737706..-4.720835 N. 1,600 valid analysis cells; outside is unaudited and transparent. Bright

NASA/JPL · Arizona State University · THEMIS daytime IR controlled mosaic v2 · NASA Mars Trek · Relative daytime infrared brightness only (qualitative): the mosaic ships no verified radiometric scaling, so no temperature, thermal-inertia, rock-abundance or dust-cover values are asserted - the legend deliberately has no units. Daytime IR mixes albedo, surface slopes, and thermophysical properties, so bright/dark patches are not by themselves a compositional or hazard classification. Not a thermal-inertia product: the TES inertia map (3 km/px) is far too coarse for this region and is not used. Display-grade: tiles nearest-neighbour resampled 1:1 from source level L=z-1 by team/gale/prepare_thermal.mjs; the ~100 m source is upsampled above z9. Source alpha is preserved. The display shares the region display-transform caveats (planetocentric display latitude on Web Mercator).

Coverage: THEMIS daytime infrared controlled mosaic v2 (Oct 2018, ~100 m/px) over the Gale Crater exploration area: derived display tiles cover 137.327-137.475 E, -4.839--4.564 N (Web-Mercator XYZ, zooms 5-9; above z9 the renderer upsamples the same source).
